markdown_report:
Select **controlled multi-negative next-item discrimination**: test supervision before adding another recent-history branch. At 0% progress, prioritize a reproducible comparison over architectural novelty.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has the weakest supplied sampled training separation: negative-beats-positive rates span 10.72–13.08%. This motivates investigation, without identifying the cause. (2) Recent-history residuals lack supplied validation evidence of improvement; training margins cannot establish generalization. (3) The stable diagnostic interface supports loss changes without inference changes. Missing gradients and unavailable metadata remain unknown.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Prakash et al. [1] report sampler-dependent accuracy and popularity disparities: more uniform negatives may reinforce shortcuts. (2) Dallmann et al. [2] show sampled/full-catalog evaluation disagreement; preserve pinned selection and qualify practical claims. (3) Oh and Cho [3] caution against excessive recency dependence. (4) Turning Dross Into Gold Loss [4] and gSASRec [5] directly precede this proposal: objective, negative count, and calibration require separate controls.

Three directions follow: discriminate among candidates, audit evaluation sensitivity, and test contextual specificity. Their framework separates changed mechanisms from evidence requirements.

| Atomic idea | Mechanism / evidence | Originality; potential; difficulty, each /10 |
|---|---|---|
| **Controlled BCE/CE × 1/32 negatives** [1,4,5] | Change supervision; select by pinned validation | 1: useful controlled application / direct precedent; 6: identifies useful settings / no new principle; 5: unchanged inference / sampling and budget controls |
| Frequency-band ranking audit [1,2] | Change diagnostic candidates only; measure rank disagreement | 3: useful synthesis / established controls; 6: exposes sensitivity / training audit lacks generalization; 4: reuse scoring / candidate bookkeeping |
| Frozen TF-IDF residual | Add title/description similarity; test lexical specificity | 3: task-specific fusion / standard representation; 5: uses available text / broad-association shortcuts; 5: no pretrained weights / serialization |

For the selected idea, retain SASRec and compare BCE versus sampled cross-entropy with K∈{1,32}. Use identical training-only exclusions, sequence-shared uniform negatives without replacement, temperature 1, valid positions, and baseline reduction. BCE is positive loss plus mean negative loss. This separates objective and count; changing sequence weighting is deferred. Keep an unchanged baseline reference if its sampler differs.

Negatives are unobserved, not confirmed dislikes. Increasing competition could improve discrimination or amplify popularity and false-negative pressure. Exclude all training positives, never held-out labels; nested negative sets support paired comparisons. Report per-category validation results and training-frequency strata when authorized outputs permit, alongside popularity and coverage diagnostics.

Predeclare feasible comparisons within remaining shared compute; report matched updates and matched GPU time. Preserve seeds, splits, all four routes, environment defaults, checkpoint rules, and predictor generation. Select only by host macro validation HR@10. Retain existing probes, add separately labeled candidate-group training ranks/loss, return null for undefined statistics, and restore module modes. Ownership, compatibility, satisfaction, and simulator traits remain unobserved.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [4] https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23; [5] https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192. No new experiments were executed.

idea.description: Keep per-dataset SASRec unchanged and test objective and negative count separately using BCE versus sampled cross-entropy with K in {1,32}. Share each sampled negative set across timesteps within a training sequence. Preserve the unchanged baseline as a reference whenever its sampling or reduction differs from these controlled conditions.
idea.motivation: Electronics repeatedly exhibits the weakest supplied training separation, while no supplied validation evidence establishes benefits from recent-history residuals. Stronger candidate competition is a feasible hypothesis, supported by direct SASRec training-objective precedents. However, the previous proposal simultaneously changed objective, negative count, sampling exclusions, and sequence weighting, preventing attribution. The revised comparison separates objective and count while fixing the remaining choices. Larger uniform-negative sets can increase computation, encourage popularity shortcuts, and penalize plausible unobserved positives; improvement remains untested.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate this experiment into the existing RecHarness sasrec_perdataset loop; the supplied functions are integration components, not a standalone train.py. Preserve the backbone, tied scoring, optimizer, initialization, batching, truncation, baseline regularization, checkpoint schedule, and baseline valid-position reduction. Inspect the supplied baseline during host implementation rather than assuming its exact loss reduction. The previous proposal's sequence-balanced averaging is withdrawn from the primary experiment because it would change user weighting; it can only be a separately budgeted control.

Define controlled conditions BCE-K1, BCE-K32, CE-K1, and CE-K32. For a valid position, BCE = softplus(-positive_logit) + mean_k softplus(negative_logit_k); CE = logsumexp([positive_logit, negative_logits]) - positive_logit. Both use raw logits, temperature 1, and the same baseline position reduction. CE-K1 is a pairwise logistic objective and is not equivalent to BCE-K1. Keep the baseline regularization coefficient fixed and report data-loss and regularization magnitudes: identical coefficients do not imply identical effective regularization across loss families. Do not tune temperature, regularization, sampler distribution, or sequence weighting within the primary factorial comparison. Call CE sampled classification, not an unbiased estimate of full-catalog softmax.

Sample one set of up to 32 unique negatives per training sequence occurrence, shared across its valid timesteps, following the granularity of the supplied direct precedent. Eligible IDs are 1 through item_count minus all distinct items in the user's complete training history. Explicitly include every current positive target in the exclusion set as a consistency check. Exclude padding. Never consult validation or test interactions. The K=1 condition uses the first item of the same randomly ordered K=32 sample; prefixes of uniform ordered samples are uniform. Sharing negatives across timesteps differs from independent per-position sampling and must be recorded. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use all available items and mask unused slots; report effective counts. If none exist, omit those positions in every controlled condition. Determine this common eligible-position mask before comparing conditions, so losses use identical examples. Preserve an unchanged baseline reference if it differs in exclusions, granularity, eligible positions, or reduction; do not attribute that comparison solely to objective or count.

For sparse exclusions, rejection-sample uniform catalog IDs, rejecting exclusions and accepted duplicates. For dense exclusions, sample from a sorted eligible complement with NumPy Generator.choice(..., replace=False), without weights. Choose between implementations using a fixed, recorded threshold based only on training data. Both must yield uniform ordered samples without replacement. Cache complements only within a declared memory limit. The reference sampler below materializes a complement for clarity; production integration may use the equivalent rejection approach. Record sampling time, duplicate-negative rate, known-training-positive collisions, and effective negative counts. Duplicates and known-positive collisions must be zero. Unknown false negatives cannot be measured from missing labels; teacher estimates would be proxies and are deferred, as introducing a teacher changes the method.

The training sampler needs user IDs and stable sequence-occurrence IDs. The diagnostic loader's leading None does not provide user identity; do not infer it from a truncated sequence. Obtain identity from the existing training dataset/sampler and keep the required diagnostic loader tuple unchanged. Derive negative-sampling randomness from seed 42, category route, epoch, stable sample ID, and occurrence index using a stable algorithm such as NumPy SeedSequence, never Python hash(). Record the numeric route mapping, NumPy version, and bit-generator type. Do not include the trial condition in this seed so controlled conditions share sampled IDs. This removes negative sampling's dependence on worker scheduling. Seed a separate torch.Generator for DataLoader ordering and initialize worker-local Python/NumPy RNGs from torch.initial_seed(); independently created generators require explicit seeds. Match backbone initialization, batch order, and ordinary-dropout streams across conditions. Loss and sampling changes must not consume the ordinary-dropout RNG stream.

Checkpoint model, optimizer, scheduler, configuration, completed epoch/update, Python and NumPy states, CPU/CUDA Torch RNG states, DataLoader generator state, sample order, and consumed position. A main-process RNG checkpoint cannot reconstruct prefetched batches or persistent-worker states. Prefer reproducible epoch-boundary resume unless consumed-order and worker/prefetch state are explicitly handled; do not claim exact mid-epoch continuation otherwise. Sampling seeds alone do not restore optimizer ordering. Save the sampler algorithm/version and condition metadata.

Predeclare trials and allocations from the actual remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, including prior attempts, diagnostics, debugging, and failures. Do not assume the full budget remains. If feasible, run all four controlled conditions with equal compute caps and retain or run the unchanged baseline reference. If only two conditions fit, prioritize BCE-K1 versus BCE-K32 to isolate count; CE-K32 then remains a deferred hypothesis, and no objective effect is claimed. Reuse an earlier baseline only if settings, checkpoints, and accounting are demonstrably comparable. Record all attempted configurations, runtime, completed epochs, and optimizer updates. Compare checkpoints at common completed updates and at equal GPU-time caps; never extrapolate missing results. Preserve the same existing checkpoint schedule and selection rule for all conditions, resolving otherwise unspecified validation ties by earliest checkpoint. Report whether category checkpoints are selected independently and apply the same rule throughout. Additional temperatures, negative counts, teacher labels, or lexical branches must replace planned work or use explicitly recorded remaining budget.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with default 200. Execute each trial on one GPU and place all artifacts beneath its trial directory. Access no hidden tests, extra datasets, or pretrained weights. Inference remains SASRec; the predictor writer must reconstruct the exact saved configuration, call eval(), and retain all four routes. Verify in-memory/exported candidate-score parity with atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5, inspect ranking discrepancies, and verify direct candidate scores against gathered full-catalog scores.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model remains the actual trained module; preserve item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data contracts. Keep existing clean loader-negative margins and directional embedding-alignment diagnostics. Add separately named fixed-candidate training loss, target rank, and negative-count diagnostics only when the appropriate training-only sampler identities are available. Do not treat loader negatives as a reconstructable user-specific exclusion set. Use eval(), no_grad(), isolated audit randomness, and a finally block restoring every submodule's prior training flag. Return null for undefined statistics or absent retained gradients; leave unavailable metadata breakdowns empty. Margins depend on logit scale and are not directly comparable as generalization measures across losses. Include finite-gradient checks during actual training rather than inventing backward-pass results in diagnosis.

Only public interaction histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions are available. Review content, ratings, item categories, prices, stores, ownership, compatibility, satisfied needs, and simulator traits must not be fabricated. Twenty real training users, five per category, still receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendation lists; these are exploratory and separate from retrospective training-target ranking audits and benchmark selection. Recommendation popularity and catalog coverage describe model outputs, not user utility.

Select only through the unchanged host benchmark: 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight four-category macro HR@10. Report per-category HR@10 when exposed. If authorized per-user target IDs and hit indicators are available, report training-frequency head/mid/tail HR@10 using frozen catalog item-count tertiles computed from training interactions only; specify tie handling, boundaries, group sizes, and empty groups. Do not alter the evaluator or request hidden labels to obtain strata. When paired outcomes exist, bootstrap users within category jointly across conditions with seed 42 and 2,000 replicates, then equally average category effects. Such intervals condition on trained checkpoints and fixed candidates and exclude training-seed variability and adaptive-selection bias. The validation sample is small and repeated selection can overfit it; limit configurations and label post-selection intervals exploratory. Sampled benchmark gains do not establish full-catalog generalization, personalized utility, or compatibility. No new performance measurements have been executed.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


# Reference implementation: use in the TRAINING sampler, where identity exists.
# route_id is a fixed documented integer for each of the four datasets.
# sample_id and occurrence are stable nonnegative integers, not Python hashes.
def sample_shared_negatives(item_count, training_items, positive_targets,
                            route_id, epoch, sample_id, occurrence, k_max=32):
    excluded = set(int(x) for x in training_items)
    excluded.update(int(x) for x in positive_targets)
    excluded.discard(0)
    eligible = np.asarray(
        [i for i in range(1, item_count + 1) if i not in excluded],
        dtype=np.int64,
    )
    rng = np.random.Generator(np.random.PCG64(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, route_id, epoch, sample_id, occurrence]
    )))
    count = min(k_max, len(eligible))
    sampled = rng.choice(eligible, size=count, replace=False)
    ids = np.zeros(k_max, dtype=np.int64)
    available = np.zeros(k_max, dtype=bool)
    ids[:count] = sampled
    available[:count] = True
    return ids, available


# Batch the reference sampler output as [B,32]. Both objectives and both
# counts reuse these ordered samples; K=1 takes their first column.
# All current positives must be present in training-only exclusions.
# This complement-based reference prioritizes clarity over large-catalog speed.


def controlled_next_item_loss(features, positive, shared_negative_ids,
                              shared_negative_valid, score_candidates,
                              objective, k, reduce_valid_positions):
    """Integration component, not a complete train.py.

    features: [B,L,D]; positive: [B,L], zero = unsupervised.
    shared_negative_ids/shared_negative_valid: [B,32].
    score_candidates(features, candidate_ids): differentiable [B,L,1+K].
    reduce_valid_positions(losses, mask): EXACT baseline data reduction,
        with the same common eligibility mask across controlled conditions.
    Baseline regularization is added separately, exactly once.
    """
    if objective not in {'bce', 'ce'} or k not in {1, 32}:
        raise ValueError('unsupported controlled condition')

    batch, length = positive.shape
    neg = shared_negative_ids[:, :k].unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, length, -1)
    available = shared_negative_valid[:, :k].bool()
    available = available.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, length, -1)
    available = available & neg.ne(0)

    # A collision is a sampler bug; do not silently change examples by loss.
    collision = available & neg.eq(positive.unsqueeze(-1)) & positive.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1)
    if collision.any():
        raise ValueError('negative collides with a training positive')
    # Sampler integration separately asserts uniqueness and exclusion of ALL
    # of the user's training positives, not merely the current target.

    valid = positive.ne(0) & available.any(dim=-1)
    if not valid.any():
        return features.sum() * 0.0

    candidates = torch.cat([positive.unsqueeze(-1), neg], dim=-1)
    logits = score_candidates(features, candidates).float()  # temperature=1
    selected = logits[valid]
    selected_available = available[valid]
    positive_logits = selected[:, 0]
    negative_logits = selected[:, 1:]

    if objective == 'bce':
        negative_terms = F.softplus(negative_logits).masked_fill(
            ~selected_available, 0.0)
        negative_mean = negative_terms.sum(-1) / selected_available.sum(-1)
        selected_losses = F.softplus(-positive_logits) + negative_mean
    else:
        selected_negative_logits = negative_logits.masked_fill(
            ~selected_available, float('-inf'))
        selected_logits = torch.cat([
            positive_logits.unsqueeze(-1), selected_negative_logits
        ], dim=-1)
        selected_losses = F.cross_entropy(
            selected_logits,
            torch.zeros(selected_logits.shape[0], dtype=torch.long,
                        device=selected_logits.device),
            reduction='none',
        )

    losses = torch.zeros_like(positive, dtype=selected_losses.dtype)
    losses = losses.masked_scatter(valid, selected_losses)
    return reduce_valid_positions(losses, valid)


# For a baseline verified to average all valid training positions:
# def reduce_valid_positions(losses, mask):
#     return losses[mask].mean()
# If the supplied baseline uses another reduction, reproduce it explicitly.
# Do not silently introduce sequence-balanced averaging.
#
# For the unchanged tied-dot-product SASRec scorer only:
# def score_candidates(features, ids):
#     return (features.unsqueeze(-2) * model.item_emb(ids)).sum(-1)
#
# Training integration:
# features = model.log2feats(sequence)
# data_loss = controlled_next_item_loss(
#     features, positive, shared_ids, shared_valid, score_candidates,
#     objective, k, baseline_reduction)
# loss = data_loss + unchanged_baseline_regularization
# optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
# loss.backward()
# check actual retained gradients for finiteness
# optimizer.step()
#
# Verify sampler exclusions, uniqueness, marginal uniformity on a small
# enumerated catalog, nested K samples, empty eligible catalogs, and shared
# timestep semantics. Check loss algebra, masking, finite gradients, and
# checkpoint/resume behavior at the supported resume boundary.
# Preserve generated predictor export and verify all-route reload parity.
# Select only through pinned host validation; audits never replace it.

originality.positive: The controlled application distinguishes objective effects from negative-count effects and corrects confounds in the earlier proposal.
originality.negative: Turning Dross Into Gold Loss and gSASRec provide direct SASRec precedents; sampled classification, multiple negatives, and factorial ablations are established.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can identify useful training settings and establish a stronger reference before architectural changes.
future_potential.negative: The proposal offers limited conceptual novelty; greater negative competition may amplify popularity shortcuts or false-negative pressure without improving practical usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The encoder and inference architecture remain unchanged, and both objectives require standard differentiable operations.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient unique sampling, stable training identities, common random samples, baseline reduction verification, reproducible loading/resumption, and compute-matched comparisons make the complete experiment more involved than a loss replacement.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): sequential-recommendation training-sampler study
contributions: The supplied research summaries report sampler-dependent aggregate accuracy and head/mid/tail behavior.
Motivates explicit sampling controls and popularity-stratified reporting.
limitations: Does not establish that increasing uniform negatives improves this benchmark.
Popularity balancing and aggregate accuracy can trade off; uniform-negative gains may conceal tail degradation.

related_work.title: Dallmann et al. (2021): sampled evaluation in sequential recommendation
contributions: Reports inconsistencies between sampled and full-catalog evaluation, including small candidate sets.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator.
Training-history ranking audits cannot establish held-out generalization.

related_work.title: Oh and Cho (2024): excessive dependence on recent interactions
contributions: Investigates excessive recency dependence and its mitigation.
limitations: Does not establish excessive recency dependence in the supplied models.
Does not imply that all recent-history pathways should be removed.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: Supports the alternative title/description specificity experiment without pretrained weights.
limitations: Lexical similarity does not establish compatibility, ownership, complementarity, or current intent.
Documentation supports implementation rather than demonstrating recommendation gains.

related_work.title: Klenitskiy and Vasilev (RecSys 2023): Turning Dross Into Gold Loss
contributions: Provides direct precedent comparing original SASRec one-negative BCE with full-catalog cross-entropy and sampled softmax using many negatives.
The supplied summary identifies sequence-shared sampled negatives, making sampling granularity an explicit implementation control.
limitations: Reported gains do not isolate every objective, negative-count, reduction, temperature, and regularization interaction.
Does not establish improvement on this pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Petrov and Macdonald (RecSys 2023): gSASRec
contributions: Studies negative sampling and overconfidence, introducing generalized BCE with increased negative counts.
Includes uniformly sampled softmax as a relevant comparison.
limitations: Does not establish that ordinary multi-negative BCE or sampled cross-entropy is optimal here.
Calibration, negative count, and objective changes require separate attribution.

related_work.title: Liu et al.: UFNRec
contributions: The supplied summary reports identifying likely false negatives and using teacher-generated soft labels.
limitations: Likely false negatives are model-based estimates rather than observed dislike labels.
Does not establish false negatives as the dominant consequence of increasing uniform-negative counts.
A teacher would add another intervention and consume additional search compute.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides additional support for qualifying conclusions drawn from sampled recommendation metrics.
limitations: Does not replace the required pinned selection protocol.
Benchmark improvements alone cannot establish full-catalog ranking improvements.

related_work.title: NumPy Generator.choice documentation
contributions: Documents uniform sampling without replacement when probability weights are omitted and replace=False.
limitations: Requires an eligible population and a sample count no larger than that population.
Materializing user-specific catalog complements can be expensive.

related_work.title: PyTorch DataLoader documentation
contributions: Documents DataLoader generators, worker initialization, and worker seed assignment.
Supports separating sample-order randomness from model randomness.
limitations: Main-process RNG restoration alone does not restore prefetched batches or persistent-worker state.
Independent NumPy generators require explicit initialization.

related_work.title: PyTorch reproducibility guidance
contributions: Explains random-source control and deterministic execution considerations.
limitations: Identical seeds do not guarantee reproducibility across software versions, platforms, or nondeterministic kernels.
Deterministic settings and software versions must be recorded alongside experiment seeds.
